core_obligations: Shrink W to a principal open subset A^d_k minus V(f) for a single polynomial f, which is legitimate because W is open and nonempty (proof lines 4650-4651).
Assume the lemma fails and conclude that f vanishes at every point of (k^sep)^d (proof lines 4652-4653).
Derive the contradiction from the infinitude of k^sep, since a nonzero polynomial in d variables over an infinite field cannot vanish on all d-tuples (proof lines 4653-4654).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a principal open subset (proof lines 4650-4651).
Assume failure and spread the vanishing of f over all of (k^sep)^d (proof lines 4652-4653).
Conclude by the infinitude of k^sep (proof lines 4653-4654).
difficulty_reason: The statement produces, in any nonempty open W of A^d_k over a field k, a closed point w with k inside kappa(w) finite separable (statement lines 4642-4647). The proof shrinks W to the complement of a single hypersurface V(f), then argues by contradiction: if no such point existed, f would vanish at every point of (k^sep)^d, which is absurd because k^sep is an infinite field (proof lines 4649-4654). The claim is H2: the only non-formal ingredient is the standard fact that a polynomial over an infinite field cannot vanish on the whole of (k^sep)^d, applied to the separable closure rather than to k.
